Guidance & outlook: And what this means for the shareholders, ROE, I think the second quarter when we have crossed 15% this quarter, FY27 first quarter, it is at 15.93% Quarterly EPS is INR25.99 per share.
And ROE, like I said earlier, is 15.93%, up 263 basis over quarter 1 of FY26.

And in this quarter, in quarter 1 of FY27, we have also added another INR26 crores to the stress NFB, taking the overall provision that is kept aside to meet the expected credit loss in kicking off next year is INR276 crores.
Growth & demand: The growth is, if I look at it, we have delivered first quarter 23% growth business growth, total business growth of 23%, which is way, way higher than the 8.82% 10-year CAGR that this bank has delivered in the past.
CASA overall, it's 16.94%, I mentioned earlier, but quarter -on-quarter, because of cur rent account de growth of 8.75%, is down 2.95%.
But when we look at it holistically, we have put th at in Slide 10, while the degrowth in CASA is just about INR500 crores.
Margins & costs: The operating profit is at INR611 crores, up 48.22%.
Net interest margin, the net interest margin is up 45 basis year- on-year, and it is now stands at 4.29% for the quarter.
So, the employee cost and the other expenses are under control, and that's what helped us to deliver an operating profit of 48.22%.
Capex & expansion: The mutual fund investment in TMB's holdings is at 0.577%.
I think we have been looking at structural changes within the bank, investing in technology, releasing the productive infrastructure precisely to generate the kind o f growth.
New software acquisition enhancement will be around 20%, 35%.
Balance sheet & cash: Cost -to-income ratio, as I just said, now stands below 40% and I've also put some kind of information on the CD ratio, on the solvency ratios, leverage ratio stands at 12.5%.

At least certainly in our book when we study the book and when we study the cash flows in the book and also our reaching out to our own customers, we are not seeing any kind of impact at all as of now.
Risks & challenges: Gross and net NPA percentage has continued to decline.
